title: Visakhapatnam Iron & Steel: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Visakhapatnam secondary steel unit buys sponge iron, scrap and billets, melts and re-rolls them into TMT bars, structurals and profiles, and sells mostly into AP and coastal construction. Cash turns on three things: power and input cost, the conversion spread per tonne, and how fast the buyer pays. **The plant is a conversion machine; the spread per tonne and the receivable days decide whether you get repaid, not the headline capacity.** RINL's Visakhapatnam Steel Plant anchors the local ecosystem and is exploring a shipping-container plant in Vizag [3]; that is a demand signal for downstream units, not a credit for RINL itself.

## What has changed now
National steel output is up only 2.4% YoY in August and 3.4% Apr-to-date [D], yet peers are printing volume-led growth with margins squeezed by coking coal and rupee depreciation [6]. JSW Steel tripled September-quarter profit on volumes and higher prices [4], and metals are the top sectoral bet this year [5]. **Read this as a volume story with a cost problem: good units run fuller, weak units bleed on input cost.** Locally, AP GST collections are -0.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], a real stress signal, while AP electricity demand is +18.1% against India +9.5% [D], a genuine tailwind for units with firm power. SEIL Vizag Profiles' expansion, at Rs 5,194 crore with 3,000 jobs [2], tells you downstream capacity is coming.

## Where to grow
Pursue re-rollers and profile makers with captive or contracted power, a named anchor buyer, and a product mix skewed to structurals and profiles rather than commodity TMT. Pursue units feeding the SEIL expansion and the container-plant supply chain [2][3]. **Avoid merchant TMT re-rollers selling spot, single-customer units, and anyone whose power is open-market.** When a proposal lands, check the power tariff contract and the top-three buyer share; if the top buyer is above half of sales, ask for a diversion-of-sales undertaking.

## How to grow safely
Structure as a cash-flow loan against receivables and inventory, not a clean term loan. Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, quarterly GST returns, and a half-yearly unit visit. **Covenant the conversion spread per tonne and receivable days; if spread falls below the sanctioned floor for two months, freeze limits.** Collect from customer the per-tonne power cost and the coking-coal sourcing mix before sanction.

## Early warning signs
- Monthly GST turnover falling two months running (monthly) -> cut limit, ask for buyer list.
- Receivable days stretching beyond sanction (monthly) -> stop fresh disbursal.
- Power bill arrears or open-market power switch (quarterly) -> reprice or exit.
- Stock build with flat sales (monthly) -> insist on stock audit.

Sources are thin on Visakhapatnam-specific steel credit data; the local items are RINL and SEIL announcements [1][2][3], and the rating reports [8][9][10][11] carry no dates, so treat them as background only.
watch: Two consecutive declines -> freeze fresh limits and request buyer-wise sales
Above sanctioned level -> stop disbursal, seek diversion undertaking
Open-market switch or arrears -> reprice or exit
Below floor for two months -> freeze limits, review pricing
Stock build with flat sales -> order stock audit
